s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute to chronic multisystem illness with neurological deterioration, fever, and mucocutaneous lesions
salient_findings: Progressive neurological decline with encephalopathy and chorea
Mucocutaneous lesions with painful vesicular oral and genital lesions
Persistent fever despite broad antimicrobial coverage
Lymphocytic pleocytosis in cerebrospinal fluid
Mesodiencephalic junction hyperintensities on MRI
key_facts: 36-year-old man with several months history of headaches, fevers, nausea, and malaise
Progressed to generalized weakness, weight loss, and altered mental status
Developed worsening encephalopathy and inability to tolerate oral intake
Subsequently developed chorea involving left upper and lower extremities
Developed painful vesicular oral and genital lesions with low-grade fever
Temperature 38.1°C at initial presentation
Leukocytosis with 21 × 10³/μL white blood cells
Elevated C-reactive protein and sedimentation rate
Mild iron deficiency anemia
Normal blood cultures, urinalysis, lactic acid, and immunologic panel
Lymphocytic pleocytosis with mixed inflammatory cells in cerebrospinal fluid
Glucose 43 mg/dL and protein 80 mg/dL in cerebrospinal fluid
Positive West Nile virus IgG, negative IgM
Negative autoimmune encephalitis panel
MRI brain findings with hyperintensities in thalami, midbrain, and pons

shortlist.label: West Nile virus neuroinvasive disease
shortlist.why_kept: Positive West Nile virus IgG and clinical presentation with encephalopathy and fever

shortlist.label: Herpes simplex virus encephalitis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of painful vesicular oral and genital lesions and encephalopathy

shortlist.label: Behçet disease
shortlist.why_kept: Mucocutaneous lesions, fever, and neurological deterioration

shortlist.label: Neurosyphilis with tabes dorsalis
shortlist.why_kept: Chorea and encephalopathy, although no clear evidence of syphilis infection

shortlist.label: Rasmussen encephalitis
shortlist.why_kept: Chorea, encephalopathy, and fever, with possible autoimmune etiology

raw.rationale: Positive West Nile virus IgG and clinical presentation of encephalopathy and hyperintensities in thalami, midbrain, and pons on MRI

rejected.label: Subacute sclerosing panencephalitis
rejected.why: Lack of measles virus infection history and absence of characteristic EEG findings

rejected.label: Herpes simplex virus encephalitis
rejected.why: Negative autoimmune encephalitis panel and absence of temporal lobe involvement on MRI

rejected.label: Behçet disease
rejected.why: Absence of intraocular lesions and lack of oral and genital ulcers at initial presentation

rejected.label: Neurosyphilis with tabes dorsalis
rejected.why: Normal immunologic panel and absence of syphilis-specific test results

rejected.label: Rasmussen encephalitis
rejected.why: Absence of focal neurologic deficits and lack of characteristic MRI findings
